title: Anchor the converted-participant guard to source instead of a per-slice state file
objective: tests/unit/test_clock_inheritance.py::test_the_participant_list_matches_the_contract read classification.PARTICIPANT_converted out of agent-state/current_contract.json -- a PER-SLICE, SINGLE-SLOT file every builder is instructed to overwrite wholesale. A permanent guard was therefore reading a scratchpad. The next slice to write its own contract would delete the block and fail the guard THROUGH THE STATE FILE with no code change, which reads as a code defect. This is an orchestration design error, not a previous builder's mistake: the single-slot rule and the guard are each correct alone and lethal together. The remedy is to remove the coupling, not to manage it.

design_decision.chosen: (a) in its SOURCE-ANCHORED form. The pinned data moves out of the volatile file entirely. The durable oracle is not a second hand-written list but THE SOURCE ITSELF: a new test derives every clock-bearing function in _AUDITED_MODULES from the AST and requires each to be classified into exactly one durable bucket -- PARTICIPANTS, _INTERNAL_CLOCK_REQUIRERS (new), or _DEFERRED_INVENTORS (existing).
design_decision.why_not_a_plain_relocated_list: Moving the contract's list into a committed file or constant next to PARTICIPANTS would leave TWO HAND-WRITTEN LISTS IN ONE PLACE, edited in one breath. That is WEAKER than the cross-artifact check it replaced. Relocation alone would satisfy the letter of the brief and lose the bite.
design_decision.why_source_is_the_right_oracle: It closes the original defect from BOTH sides. Drop a participant from PARTICIPANTS and it surfaces in the derived REQUIRED set with no bucket. Re-optionalise it as well -- the RELOCATOR move that forwards None onward and that every other guard in this file is blind to -- and it surfaces in the derived OPTIONAL set as an undocumented deferral. Both were measured, not argued.
design_decision.precedent_already_in_the_file: _DEFERRED_INVENTORS is already a durable, test-owned, hand-maintained ledger checked in BOTH directions against source ('the allowance must not outlive the deferral it documents'). The remedy follows a pattern this file already trusts rather than inventing one.
design_decision.alternative_REJECTED_(c): Making current_contract.json explicitly two-part -- a per-slice section overwritten and a durable section carried forward -- was rejected on two grounds. First, enforcing it requires a NEW permanent test that reads the same volatile file, taking the count of permanent tests coupled to a per-slice scratchpad from ONE to TWO; it manages the coupling instead of removing it. Second, the durable-section test can only ever assert PRESENCE, and a builder satisfies presence by pasting a stale block -- which is precisely the drift the guard exists to catch. A rule of the form 'overwrite this file except for the parts you must not' IS the invisible coupling that caused the incident.
design_decision.alternative_RULED_OUT_BY_THE_ORCHESTRATO: Skip-when-absent. Not proposed. It trades a confusing failure for a SILENT GAP and would fail open exactly when a builder had overwritten the block.
design_decision.reasoning_written_into_the_source: The full rationale, including why the file is no longer read, lives in the new test's docstring so the next reader does not reintroduce the coupling.

verification_method.baseline_rule: A baseline must be shown to have EXECUTED at least one test, not merely to have exited 0. The runner parses `collected N`, ABORTS below an explicitly-passed floor, and treats pytest exit 5 as NOTHING COLLECTED and aborts separately. Every -k run carries a floor for this reason.
verification_method.mutation_rule: Every mutation is PROVEN on disk before its measurement is believed: exact search text present exactly the expected number of times before, absent/replaced after, and `git diff --numstat` non-empty. Restoration is verified by comparing `git hash-object` against `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`. An unapplied mutation reads exactly like a surviving one.
verification_method.mutation_must_restore_the_DEFECT: The load-bearing mutation is the RELOCATOR (required clock -> optional, forwarding None onward with no `or` fallback), because that is the shape the other guards are blind to. Deleting an argument would kill on arity and prove nothing about behaviour.
verification_method.environment_rule: Preconditions ASSERTED not announced: python and pytest versions read with checked exit codes, and the baseline shown to collect 2998 and execute 2709 before any change was made.
verification_method.skip_is_not_a_pass: 289 integration tests skip without DATABASE_URL. Recorded on every run so a skipped suite can never be mistaken for a green one.
verification_method.powershell_trap: Select-Object -First/-Last corrupts $LASTEXITCODE. Exit codes are read from BARE calls only.
verification_method.database: NONE. This slice needed no PostgreSQL: the affected module imports app packages and parses source with ast. No container was created, so none was removed.

predictions_frozen_before_measurement.P2_CONFIRMED: Deleting the classification block fails exactly one test and no other. 1 failed / 2708 passed / 2998 collected.
predictions_frozen_before_measurement.P4_CONFIRMED: The full original defect is otherwise SILENT: under the RELOCATOR mutation, 1 failed / 2707 passed / 2997 collected. Exactly one test in the repository stands between this codebase and that defect.
predictions_frozen_before_measurement.P5_FALSIFIED_AS_PREDICTED: I predicted at LOW confidence that deriving 'functions with a required clock' would NOT yield exactly the 7 participants. It yields 11. Pure derivation is therefore NOT a usable sole oracle, which is why the remedy is closure-into-buckets rather than equality-with-a-derived-set.
predictions_frozen_before_measurement.ERROR_I_MADE_AND_CAUGHT: M2 (adding a non-participant to the pinned list) was killed by a PRE-EXISTING guard, not mine. Investigating why exposed a real gap: a participant pinned from a module OUTSIDE _AUDITED_MODULES is invisible to the closure loop, which only visits audited modules. Added an explicit scope assertion and re-ran the mutation with -k to prove the new guard fires INDEPENDENTLY. Found by mutation, not by reasoning.

required_evaluation_level_reason: Test-only change under tests/unit. No production code, no schema, no Z0 classification logic, no security boundary, no public workflow, so the mandatory Level-2 list in docs/AGENT_HARNESS.md does not apply. STATED PLAINLY: the test being restructured is itself a guard over Z0 clock correctness, so a reviewer should check the guard was not BLUNTED. That is why 'the guard still bites' is an acceptance criterion proven by mutation rather than by greenness, and why the RELOCATOR mutation -- not an arity break -- is the evidence offered.
